problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-4,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=-2+t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=5\end{aligned}.$
worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-4,1⟩.$  From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨1,4,0⟩.$  So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨1,4,0⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =⟨2,-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14 \\ x+4y & =-14 \\ x+4y+14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
